---
title: "From a STAC catalogue"
---



When a collection is catalogued with the
[projection](https://github.com/stac-extensions/projection) and
[raster](https://github.com/stac-extensions/raster) STAC extensions, the
catalogue already says everything the VRT needs. `from_stac()` uses it
directly and opens no file:

| VRT element | catalogue field |
|---|---|
| grid (dims, x/y coordinates) | `proj:shape`, `proj:transform` |
| `<SRS>` | `proj:epsg` / `proj:code` / `proj:wkt2` |
| time coordinate | item `datetime` |
| one array per asset | asset keys with `raster:bands` |
| dtype, nodata, scale, offset, unit | `raster:bands[0]` |
| sources | asset `href`, placed at the item's time position |

::: {#1450b3d0 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
from xvrt import from_stac
from _fixtures import geotiffs, WKT_4326

tifs = geotiffs(n=3)
items = [
    {
        "id": f"day{i}",
        "properties": {
            "datetime": f"2026-01-0{i + 1}T00:00:00Z",
            "proj:shape": [3, 4],
            "proj:transform": [1.0, 0, 145.0, 0, -1.0, -42.0, 0, 0, 1],
            "proj:wkt2": WKT_4326,
        },
        "assets": {
            "analysed_sst": {
                "href": str(p),
                "raster:bands": [{"data_type": "int16", "nodata": -32768,
                                  "scale": 0.001, "offset": 25.0, "unit": "celsius"}],
            }
        },
    }
    for i, p in enumerate(tifs)
]
out = from_stac(items, tifs[0].parent / "catalogue.vrt")

from osgeo import gdal
gdal.UseExceptions()
a = gdal.OpenEx(str(out), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER).GetRootGroup().OpenMDArray("analysed_sst")
print([d.GetSize() for d in a.GetDimensions()], a.GetScale(), a.GetOffset(), a.GetUnit())
a.GetUnscaled().ReadAsArray()[:, 0, :]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
[3, 3, 4] 0.001 25.0 celsius
```
:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
```
array([[12.  , 12.05, 12.1 , 12.15],
       [12.1 , 12.15, 12.2 , 12.25],
       [12.2 , 12.25, 12.3 , 12.35]])
```
:::
:::


`items` may be a list of STAC item dicts (nested `properties` or flat
stac-geoparquet rows; `pystac.Item` objects work too) or the path or URL of a
stac-geoparquet file.

## What it checks

The catalogue is trusted, but not blindly:

- **One grid.** Items on different grids are refused (no resampling).
- **One item per time.** Duplicate datetimes are refused.
- **One storage description per asset.** If dtype, nodata, scale or offset
  change between items the asset is refused, because one array needs one
  decoding. A unit missing from some items is filled from the others;
  conflicting units warn and use the most common.
- **Missing assets are gaps.** An item without an asset leaves nodata at its
  time position, so a variable that starts later than the others needs no
  special handling.

The template Dataset it builds uses zero-memory placeholders
(`numpy.broadcast_to`), so a catalogue of thousands of full-resolution days
costs nothing to describe. See the [GHRSST MUR example](../examples/ghrsst-mur.qmd)
for 8913 days of five variables.
